done_when: init.protect drops required checks that no remaining workflow produces, names the repo from the origin remote explicitly in every gh api call, and a test proves each

findings.body: The scanner only recognizes the exact line `jobs:` and fixed two-space indentation. With `jobs: # required checks` in the deleted workflow, it discovers no removed jobs, leaving `old-check` and `lint` required and blocking later PRs. The same formatting in a surviving workflow can instead remove a live requirement. These are ordinary valid [GitHub workflow YAML](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax). Handle comments and valid indentation, and extend the command-level regression test to cover them.

findings.body: An absolute local origin bypasses the refusal and restores `{owner}/{repo}` in both protection requests. With another GitHub remote or `GH_REPO` configured, those requests can modify an unrelated repository: [gh resolves these placeholders from its repository context](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api). This production exception exists to accommodate test fixtures. Remove it and use explicit GitHub fetch URLs with local push URLs in those fixtures, as the new test already does at tests/test_fix_forge_s_branch_protection_keeps_required.py:65–66.
findings.title: Simpler: test-only repository fallback → refuse unresolved origins

why: Forge's branch protection keeps required checks whose workflows a migration deletes, which blocks every later pull request once admins are enforced, and with two remotes and no gh default it can protect the wrong repo
